summary.question: Who are we?
summary.answer: Crewola for Home Services is a managed workflow service for home-service companies and their trade teams that turns plumbing, HVAC, electrical and roofing enquiries into organised quote requests, appointment proposals and follow-ups, within the rules your team sets. Every enquiry is captured and moved to a booking or quote request, and pricing and dispatch need human approval.
takeaways: Every enquiry is captured and moved to a booking or quote request.
Diagnosis, safety decisions, binding quotes, discounts and dispatch commitments stay with qualified or authorised staff.
Pricing and dispatch need human approval.
Results are measured by enquiries reaching a confirmed next step, compared with how you work today.

scope.covers: Plumbing, HVAC, electrical and roofing enquiries turned into visit requests, quote requests and follow-ups, for the trade teams and enquiry channels you choose.
scope.excludes: Diagnosis, safety decisions, repair instructions, binding quotes, discounts, dispatch commitments and live emergency response.
scope.instead: Those go to your dispatcher, estimator or duty contact. Urgent issues follow your business emergency protocol.

statement: Your team has jobs to finish.
Keep new enquiries, quote requests and scheduling handoffs moving while your crew is on site.

workflow.heading: The next job starts with a clear brief.
workflow.body: A call comes in while the crew is busy. Someone needs to collect the details, check the service area and make sure the enquiry reaches the right person.

steps.title: Collect the job details
steps.body: Capture the requested trade, location, issue and preferred timing from an approved enquiry source.

steps.title: Prepare the handoff
steps.body: Check agreed service-area and scheduling rules. Prepare a quote request or appointment proposal.

steps.title: Confirm and follow up
steps.body: Keep pricing and dispatch decisions with your team. Track the enquiry until its next step is confirmed.

demo.heading: From enquiry to an agreed next step.
demo.body: Explore routine booking, quote preparation and urgent escalation. Each example shows a proposed handoff, using synthetic information.

scenes.request: My outdoor tap is leaking. Could you come tomorrow?
scenes.rule: Check service area and availability. A proposed slot is not a confirmed visit.
scenes.draft: Collect address and job details, then prepare a visit request for dispatcher approval.
scenes.result: Scheduling handoff prepared. Arrival time and availability remain unconfirmed.

scenes.request: Can you quote for replacing our roof?
scenes.rule: An estimate requires approved pricing and sufficient scope. Do not invent a binding price.
scenes.draft: Collect property details and requested work; ask the estimator whether a site inspection is needed.
scenes.result: Estimator handoff prepared. No binding quote or inspection date was promised.

scenes.request: There is a burning smell near the electrical panel.
scenes.rule: Escalate immediately under the business emergency protocol. Do not give repair instructions or promise availability.
scenes.draft: Flag urgent human review and display the business-approved emergency guidance.
scenes.result: Urgent escalation illustrated. This demo provides no live emergency response.

faq.a: Plumbing, HVAC, electrical and roofing are the candidate use cases. Each workflow follows the business’s own service-area, scheduling and escalation rules.

faq.q: Will it produce a binding quote?
faq.a: No. Only approved pricing and permitted actions can be included in the agreed workflow; complex scope, inspections and price exceptions go to your estimator.

faq.q: Can customers use this for emergencies?
faq.a: No. This marketing page is not an emergency service. A customer-facing deployment needs explicit urgent escalation procedures and business-approved guidance.
